# FUSE — White-label Music Player UI/UX Fusion

**A complete SVG-first design specification inspired by classic Winamp, VOX for macOS, and AIMP**

Version 1.0 · Design study and implementation handoff · 25 November 2026

> **One player. Three lineages. No borrowed branding.** FUSE combines Winamp’s modular performance controls and skin culture, VOX’s compact album-led restraint, and AIMP’s deep library, queue, tagging, and audio tooling. The result is an original, white-label product system—not a reproduction of any reference application.

## Download and reading guide

- **This document is the primary deliverable.** It contains the full analysis, specifications, wireframes, screen designs, component sheets, skin contract, and implementation guidance.
- Artwork is embedded as self-contained SVG data URIs; no network connection is required to view the images in a compatible Markdown renderer.
- Every illustration also has an editable SVG source in the companion `svg/` directory and a full SVG source listing in Appendix A of this document.
- `FUSE-Design-Gallery.html` is an optional visual companion with an index and full-size artwork. `FUSE-Waveform-Lab.html` is an optional interactive SVG/audio-analysis demonstration.
- The ZIP package contains this Markdown, all SVGs, the gallery, the demo, tokens, schema, and generation scripts.

**Status:** high-fidelity design specification and vector prototype, not a shipped audio engine. Static SVG frames illustrate reactive layouts; the separate waveform lab demonstrates actual audio-driven SVG updates. Backend capabilities, native integrations, licensing, and user-test results are explicitly marked as pending rather than claimed.

**Fictional content:** Northbound, Afterglow, Slow satellites, and the other track/artist names are demonstration data. All album sleeves, icons, waveforms, textures, and layouts in the package are original vector artwork. No Winamp sprites, VOX assets, AIMP skins, or reference-product logos are included.

## 1. Executive decision

### The fusion in one sentence

**A calm, album-led listening workspace that can expand into a powerful audio workstation, shrink into a compact performance player, and change its entire visual signature without changing how it behaves.**

### What belongs to each lineage

| Lineage | Adopted strength | Modernized expression |
|---|---|---|
| Classic Winamp | Immediate transport, visible spectrum, modular player/EQ/playlist stack, skin identity | Original vector metal skin, readable labels, modern target sizes, shared state across modules |
| VOX for macOS | Compact footprint, artwork-first hierarchy, restrained controls, source-format awareness | Persistent now-playing identity, quiet chrome, explicit quality badges, mini/shade modes |
| AIMP | Library depth, explicit queue, smart playlists, tagging, DSP, flexible skins | Task-grouped navigation, safe batch editing, capability-aware audio settings, tokenized skin system |

### The non-negotiable product rules

1. **Playback is always recoverable.** Play/pause, track identity, and an exit from compact/focus modes remain reachable.
2. **Queue is explicit.** “Play next,” playlist context, selection, and history are different objects with different visual treatments.
3. **Power is progressive.** A new user can import and play without understanding DSP, exclusive output, or skin tokens.
4. **Quality claims are precise.** Source format, processing state, and negotiated output are separate facts.
5. **Skins cannot break usability.** Color, texture, and approved layout variants are customizable; control meaning, focus, targets, and error honesty are not.
6. **Motion is optional.** Reactive visuals are pausable and have a static presentation; reduced motion is respected.
7. **Local files are safe.** Import does not modify files; tag writes, deletion, and renaming are separate explicit operations.
8. **Every state tells the truth.** Loading, buffering, paused, stopped, unavailable, and error are not interchangeable.

### Immediate visual signature

- Graphite surfaces, mint interaction accent, warm amber secondary accent, and original ocean/sun album geometry.
- A persistent bottom transport in workspace mode; a compact stacked transport in Classic mode.
- Mirrored waveform bars as the default signal, with spectrum, oscilloscope, and static alternatives.
- Strong title hierarchy, tabular time/quality numerals, restrained borders, and generous regional spacing.
- No neon-only meaning, no tiny legacy hit targets, no decorative fake meters, and no account wall for local playback.

## 2. Reference-product analysis

### 2.1 Evidence boundary

This analysis uses public product pages, official help/documentation where available, and representative screenshots. It is a **design-direction analysis**, not a controlled benchmark or a claim that every feature was tested in every current version. VOX premium gating, AIMP platform/plugin support, and Winamp version differences can change. The fusion therefore treats advanced capabilities as backend-advertised options rather than universal promises.

### 2.2 Classic Winamp

**Observed strengths**

- The player, equalizer, and playlist form a recognizable modular stack; the user can see the performance tools at once.
- Transport, position, spectrum, and track identity are close together, supporting glanceable control.
- Classic skins make the player feel personal and culturally recognizable.
- Windowshade/compact behavior anticipates a small always-available player.
- Official desktop help describes playlist, EQ, skin, and color-theme options, alongside classic and modern skin support. [4](https://support.winamp.com/winamp-desktop-player-for-windows)
- Classic skin configuration separates visualization colors and playlist colors into editable text mappings. [6](https://winampskins.neocities.org/config)

**Shortcomings to avoid**

- Tiny bitmap-era controls and dense labels do not scale well to modern accessibility, touch, or high-zoom requirements.
- Icon-only or abbreviated controls can hide meaning from new users.
- Beveled surfaces and spectral color can compete with content if copied literally.
- Legacy skin portability is not the same as a safe, semantic, cross-platform skin contract.
- A fixed miniature canvas should not dictate modern minimum target sizes.

**Fusion decisions**

- Keep the **module grammar**: player → EQ → playlist, with a compact stack and a shade strip.
- Replace copied sprites with original vector bevels, gradients, and textures.
- Keep spectral energy but use a calmer palette and explicit mode labels.
- Preserve the cultural feeling of ownership without preserving 275-pixel-wide interaction constraints.
- Make Classic a presentation mode, not a separate playback implementation.

### 2.3 VOX for macOS

**Observed strengths**

- The public Mac page presents a compact, artwork-led player with format information and a restrained control surface. [1](https://vox.rocks/mac-music-player)
- The product emphasizes local/lossless and hi-res playback, EQ, gapless behavior, output settings, and multiple sources. [1](https://vox.rocks/mac-music-player)
- A small player can remain useful without turning into a full library browser.
- Source-format awareness is valuable to users who care about fidelity.

**Shortcomings to avoid**

- Compactness can hide queue context, advanced state, and the difference between source and output.
- Premium/source/cloud features can blur the boundary between a local player and a service.
- A minimalist surface may leave batch organization and recovery flows under-explained.
- Mac-specific output behavior should not be assumed on Windows, Linux, web, or mobile.

**Fusion decisions**

- Use artwork and track identity as the emotional center of Now Playing.
- Keep mini and shade modes genuinely small, but preserve identity, transport, and expansion.
- Show source quality as a badge and put detailed facts in Track Details.
- Keep local playback account-free in the proposed product; remote providers are optional extensions.
- Do not equate “24/96 source” with “24/96 currently reaching the device.”

### 2.4 AIMP

**Observed strengths**

- Official feature documentation covers multiple playlists, explicit playback queue, smart playlists, grouping, search, and per-playlist view settings. [2](https://www.aimp.ru/?do=features)
- The same documentation describes a 20-band EQ, effects, normalization, mixing options, library statistics, tag editing, chapters, and scheduling. [2](https://www.aimp.ru/?do=features)
- Skin transformers and high-DPI support demonstrate that depth and visual flexibility can coexist. [2](https://www.aimp.ru/?do=features)
- AIMP’s ecosystem treats organization and audio processing as first-class tasks rather than afterthoughts.

**Shortcomings to avoid**

- Feature breadth can produce dense settings trees and competing panels.
- Queue, playlist, selection, and library actions need explicit language to avoid accidental destructive operations.
- Advanced DSP and output options can intimidate users or imply fidelity guarantees that depend on the backend.
- A Windows-centered toolset should not be presented as identical across platforms.

**Fusion decisions**

- Adopt the **capability breadth**, not the density: Library, Playlists, Sound Studio, Skin Studio, and Settings are separate task groups.
- Make queue order and resume context visible in the same panel.
- Use numeric EQ values, presets, reset, and a processing-chain summary.
- Expose advanced output only when supported; explain route changes and processing effects.
- Keep batch tag editing explicit, reversible where possible, and separate from file renaming.

### 2.5 Cross-product decision matrix

| Aspect | Winamp contribution | VOX contribution | AIMP contribution | FUSE resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First impression | Performance identity | Calm artwork-led compactness | Functional breadth | Album-led workspace; tools one click away |
| Transport | Immediate and modular | Minimal | Feature-complete | Persistent shared transport; compact variant |
| Queue | Playlist adjacency | Compact context | Explicit queue | Separate “Play next” and “Then resumes at” regions |
| Library | Playlist editor | Source switching | Deep organization | Albums/tracks/artists/folders + smart playlists |
| EQ | Visible sliders | Approachable presets | Deep DSP | 10-band default; advanced chain capability-gated |
| Visualizer | Spectrum culture | Subtle presence | Flexible display | Four honest modes, pausable, SVG-driven |
| Skins | Strong identity | Restraint | Transformers | Semantic tokens + approved layout variants |
| Quality | Format readout | Hi-res awareness | Processing depth | Source / DSP / output facts separated |
| Accessibility | Needs modernization | Needs explicit depth | Needs progressive disclosure | Targets, focus, contrast, motion, and semantics locked |
| Safety | Legacy destructive ambiguity | Service boundary | Batch-operation risk | Explicit queue removal, tag save, and file deletion boundaries |

## 3. Scope, assumptions, personas, and success criteria

### 3.1 Proposed product scope

**Core v1 design scope:** local audio import and playback; library; playlists; explicit queue; favorites/history; search; track details; lyrics import; EQ and presets; output selection; sleep timer; mini/shade/focus modes; skins; accessibility; recovery; privacy controls.

**Conditional extensions:** radio/podcasts, network renderers, cloud sources, scrobbling, artwork lookup, CD tools, conversion, recording, exclusive/bit-perfect output, DSD, advanced DSP, mobile native integration. These require backend capability checks, permissions, and separate validation. They are not implied by the core SVG screens.

**Platform assumption:** desktop-first product with a responsive web/desktop implementation path and conceptual mobile layouts. Native window chrome, media keys, file permissions, safe areas, and audio-session behavior belong to the host integration layer.

### 3.2 Personas

| Persona | Primary job | What must be effortless | What must not happen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Casual listener | Play a local album | Import, play, pause, next, volume | Forced account, confusing queue, hidden exit |
| Collector | Organize a large library | Search, filter, batch tags, playlists | Silent file changes, mixed-value overwrite |
| Audiophile | Understand and shape output | Source facts, EQ, output route, gain | False bit-perfect claims, clipping surprises |
| Classic-player fan | Keep a compact performance player | Stack, shade, spectrum, skins | Tiny targets, lost queue when resizing |
| Keyboard/AT user | Operate without sighted pointer use | Focus, names, values, announcements | Icon-only meaning, focus traps, motion overload |
| White-label partner | Ship a branded player | Tokens, logo slot, skin validation | Brand colors breaking contrast or behavior |

### 3.3 Success criteria and measurement plan

These are **target thresholds for usability testing**, not results already achieved.

- First local track plays after a deliberate import/open action; measure completion and time on task.
- At least 90% of test participants can distinguish “Play next” from playlist context after one explanation.
- No critical task requires horizontal scrolling at the compact reference width or 200% text size.
- All core controls have accessible names, roles, states, and keyboard operation.
- A skin with failing contrast cannot be applied without an explicit, informed override; default skins must pass.
- Queue and playback state survive mode changes and ordinary restarts according to settings.
- Error recovery never silently deletes files or clears the queue.
- Visualizer pause stops visual updates without pausing audio.

## 4. Gap analysis and risk register

| ID | Gap / risk | Consequence | Design mitigation | Validation / owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G01 | Source vs output quality conflation | Misleading fidelity claims | Separate badges and facts; processing summary | Audio engine + QA |
| G02 | Queue vs playlist ambiguity | Wrong next track; accidental removal | Explicit queue panel and resume context | UX test + state tests |
| G03 | Feature density | New-user confusion | Progressive disclosure; task-grouped settings | Tree test + first-run test |
| G04 | Legacy compact targets | Motor/accessibility failure | 40/44 px defaults; minimum 24 px | Accessibility audit |
| G05 | Skin breaks contrast/focus | Unusable branded product | Token validation and locked invariants | Automated skin tests |
| G06 | Fake reactive visuals | Loss of trust | Static frames labeled; live demo uses analyser | Signal-state tests |
| G07 | Motion overload | Distraction or adverse reaction | Pause/static mode; reduced-motion default | WCAG review + user test |
| G08 | Batch tag overwrite | Data loss | Mixed values; explicit save; preview | File-operation tests |
| G09 | Unsupported backend toggle | Broken promise | Capability registry; hide/explain unavailable | Platform integration tests |
| G10 | Remote/local boundary blur | Privacy surprise | Local-first defaults; opt-in providers | Privacy review |
| G11 | Stream treated as file | Broken seek/duration UI | Stream-specific state and disabled seek | Radio/stream tests |
| G12 | Mode change loses state | User disorientation | Shared store; mode is presentation only | Integration tests |
| G13 | Long metadata overflow | Hidden identity/actions | Truncation + full details; stable action slots | Long-string/RTL tests |
| G14 | Modal hides recovery | Trapped user | Focus trap, Esc, cancel, persistent errors | Keyboard/AT tests |
| G15 | SVG-only production semantics | Screen-reader failure | SVG presentation + native/HTML control layer | AT smoke tests |
| G16 | Skin code execution | Security risk | Data-only skins; no scripts/external fetch | Schema/security review |
| G17 | Large library performance | UI stalls | Virtualized lists; incremental indexing | 100k-track benchmark |
| G18 | Audio/visual thread contention | Dropouts or jank | Audio thread isolated; bounded visual work | Performance profiling |
| G19 | Offline source ambiguity | Dead controls | Available/unavailable badges; local fallback | Disconnect tests |
| G20 | Unclear destructive scope | File deletion fear | “Remove from playlist” vs “Delete file” labels | Copy review + confirmation test |

### Known limitations of this deliverable

- No production audio decoder, database, native file-permission layer, or platform media-session integration is implemented.
- No formal usability study, screen-reader certification, or WCAG conformance audit has been performed.
- The waveform lab is a demonstration using browser audio analysis; it is not a reference DSP implementation.
- Mobile screens are design concepts; native gesture, safe-area, and background-audio behavior remain implementation work.
- Advanced AIMP-like tools are inventoried and gated, not all given full production screens in v1.

## 5. Feature inventory and priority model

**P0** = required for a coherent local player; **P1** = strong differentiator; **P2** = conditional extension; **R** = research before commitment.

| Area | Feature | Priority | UI surface | Dependency / note |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Playback | Open files/folders; play/pause/stop; previous/next; seek; volume/mute | P0 | Transport, import, dialogs | Decoder and host file access |
| Playback | Shuffle; repeat off/all/one; gapless where supported | P0/P1 | Transport, settings | Gapless is capability-gated |
| Playback | Resume track/position; restore queue | P1 | Settings + startup | Persisted state |
| Queue | Play next; add to queue; reorder; remove; clear; undo | P0 | Queue panel/sheet | Explicit queue store |
| Queue | Resume visible playlist context | P0 | Queue panel | Context pointer |
| Library | Index folders; incremental scan; cancel; partial results | P0 | Import, library settings | Non-destructive indexing |
| Library | Albums/tracks/artists/folders; grid/list; sort/filter | P0 | Library | Database + virtualization |
| Library | Search across local metadata | P0 | Global search | Scoped query; no implicit remote |
| Playlists | Multiple playlists; create/rename/duplicate; M3U/M3U8 export | P0/P1 | Playlists | Path portability policy |
| Playlists | Smart playlists with readable rules | P1 | Playlist builder | Query engine |
| Organization | Favorites; ratings; history; play counts | P1 | Library/history | Local metadata/store |
| Metadata | Single/batch tags; mixed values; artwork; explicit save | P1 | Tag editor | Format-specific write support |
| Metadata | File rename preview; chapter/CUE editing | P2 | Advanced tools | Separate destructive preview |
| Sound | 10-band EQ; preamp; presets; reset; numeric values | P0/P1 | Sound studio | DSP backend |
| Sound | ReplayGain/normalization; clipping protection | P1 | Settings + chain | Measurement and limiter |
| Sound | Crossfeed; tempo/pitch; effects; 20-band EQ | P2 | Advanced sound | Capability-gated |
| Output | Device chooser; route-change warning | P0/P1 | Output dialog | Host audio API |
| Output | Exclusive/bit-perfect; DSD; multichannel | P2/R | Capabilities | Backend + device negotiation |
| Visuals | Waveform/spectrum/oscilloscope/static; pause | P0/P1 | Signal region/focus view | Analysis data; reduced motion |
| Modes | Workspace; focus; mini; shade; Classic stack | P1 | Mode switcher | Shared state |
| Skins | Dark/light/high-contrast/Classic; token editor; import | P1 | Skin studio | Data-only schema + validation |
| Accessibility | Keyboard map; focus; zoom; reduced motion; AT semantics | P0 | Everywhere | Native/HTML control layer |
| Comfort | Sleep timer with fade/pause outcome | P1 | Timer dialog | No implicit system shutdown |
| Information | Track facts; embedded/local lyrics; LRC | P1 | Track details | No automatic remote fetch |
| Recovery | Missing file; decode error; permissions; offline; retry | P0 | Alerts/recovery screens | Preserve queue/library |
| Privacy | Source-folder control; export; clear history/cache | P0/P1 | Settings | Non-destructive data controls |
| Remote | Saved radio URLs; podcasts; reconnect | P2 | Radio/podcasts | Stream semantics; permissions |
| Remote | Cloud/artwork/scrobbling/providers | P2/R | Integrations | Opt-in; privacy review |
| Tools | Converter; CD rip; recording; scheduler shutdown | P2/R | Advanced tools | Legal/platform/backend review |

### Progressive disclosure policy

- **Level 1 — Listen:** import, play, pause, next, volume, queue, search.
- **Level 2 — Organize:** playlists, favorites, history, tags, smart rules.
- **Level 3 — Shape:** EQ, presets, normalization, output, timer, skins.
- **Level 4 — Extend:** providers, advanced DSP, exclusive output, conversion, recording.

A feature never appears as an enabled control merely because a reference product has it. The capability registry determines whether it is available, unavailable with explanation, or hidden because the platform cannot support it.

## 6. Information architecture and navigation

### Primary navigation

```text
FUSE shell
├── Now playing
│   ├── Performance / artwork / signal
│   ├── Explicit queue preview
│   └── Track details / lyrics
├── Library
│   ├── Albums
│   ├── Tracks
│   ├── Artists
│   └── Folders
├── Playlists
│   ├── Standard playlists
│   ├── Smart playlists
│   └── Playlist builder
├── Favorites
├── History
├── Radio / Podcasts [conditional]
├── Sound studio
│   ├── EQ / presets
│   ├── Processing chain
│   └── Output capabilities
├── Skin studio
│   ├── Installed skins
│   ├── Token editor
│   └── Import / validation
└── Settings
    ├── Audio
    ├── Library / sources
    ├── Appearance / accessibility
    ├── Shortcuts
    └── Privacy / data
```

### Navigation rules

- Desktop ≥1200 px: persistent labeled sidebar; content and queue may coexist.
- 900–1199 px: labeled horizontal tabs; queue becomes a panel/sheet when space is insufficient.
- <900 px: single-column content; persistent mini transport; queue is a labeled sheet.
- Mobile: bottom navigation only when it does not compete with the mini player; otherwise labeled header tabs and a back stack.
- Sound Studio, Skin Studio, and Settings are reachable from the header and command search; they are not buried inside Now Playing.
- Active navigation is indicated by tint **and** position/weight; focus is a separate ring.
- Core destinations are not disabled when empty; they open useful empty states.

### Search and command behavior

- `Ctrl/⌘+F` focuses local search. Results are grouped by type: artist, album, track, playlist, station.
- Typing never triggers playback. Enter opens the highlighted result; an explicit Play action starts audio.
- Remote search is labeled and opt-in. Offline remote results are marked unavailable.
- Search preserves the player and explicit queue. Closing search returns focus to the invoking control.
- Recent searches are local and clearable; no query is sent to a provider without consent.

## 7. Core object model and playback semantics

### 7.1 Separate objects

| Object | Meaning | Visual treatment | Typical actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Library item | Indexed audio file and metadata | Normal row/card | Play, queue, favorite, edit |
| Playback context | Ordered source: album, playlist, folder | “Playing from …” header | Play context, shuffle context |
| Current track | Audio actually playing or paused | Accent title + signal icon | Pause, seek, details |
| Explicit queue | User-added future items overriding context | “Up next” panel + order | Reorder, remove, clear |
| Selection | Rows targeted by a batch action | Checkbox + selection tint | Queue, playlist, tags |
| Favorite | User-marked item independent of playback | Heart/state label | Toggle favorite |
| History | Record of past playback | Timestamped list | Replay, queue, clear |
| Stream | Remote live source | Buffering/live badge | Retry, stop; no file seek |

### 7.2 Queue algorithm (specified behavior)

1. Playing a context sets `contextId`, `contextOrder`, and `contextIndex`; it does not silently copy the entire library into the explicit queue.
2. “Play next” inserts after the current item in the explicit queue. “Add to queue” appends.
3. At track end, consume the first explicit queue item if one exists.
4. When the explicit queue is empty, advance the context according to shuffle/repeat settings.
5. Removing a queued item changes only the queue. Undo restores its position if the surrounding context is still valid.
6. Clearing the queue leaves the current track and context intact; show the resume point.
7. If the resume item is unavailable, enter recovery and preserve the remaining context.
8. Shuffle affects context traversal, not the user’s explicit queue order, unless the user explicitly chooses “Shuffle queue.”
9. Repeat One repeats the current track only when the explicit queue is empty; otherwise the queue still advances. This rule must be explained in the repeat tooltip.
10. Mode changes never mutate queue order.

### 7.3 Playback state machine

```text
empty ──open/import──> ready
ready ──play──> loading ──success──> playing
loading ──failure──> error
loading ──cancel──> ready
playing ──pause──> paused ──play──> playing
playing ──buffer underrun──> buffering ──data──> playing
playing/paused ──stop──> stopped
playing/paused ──end──> next decision
next decision ──queue item──> loading
next decision ──context item──> loading
next decision ──no next──> stopped
error ──locate/retry──> loading
error ──skip──> next decision
buffering ──retry exhausted──> error
```

**UI truth table**

| State | Primary button | Signal | Seek | Queue | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty | Disabled Play with explanation | Static placeholder | Disabled | No context | Import/open |
| Loading | Cancel/back where safe | Static + progress | Disabled until duration known | Target visible | Timeout/retry |
| Playing | Pause | Live or paused visuals | Enabled for seekable media | Current marked | Pause/next |
| Paused | Play | Frozen frame | Enabled | Position retained | Resume |
| Buffering | Pause/skip | Last frame + label | Only if stream semantics allow | Honest position | Retry/local |
| Stopped | Play from start | Static art | Reset/disabled by policy | Context retained | Choose track |
| Error | Retry only if safe | No fake live signal | Disabled | Preserved | Locate/skip/diagnostics |
| Offline | Local playback enabled | Local only | Local rules | Remote marked unavailable | Retry remote later |

### 7.4 Quality and processing model

- `source`: codec, sample rate, bit depth, channels, bitrate, duration, file size, ReplayGain tags.
- `processing`: EQ enabled, preamp, normalization, crossfeed, limiter, effects, measured gain changes.
- `output`: selected device, negotiated format, exclusive/shared mode, channel mapping, backend status.

The UI displays source badges by default. A “bit-perfect” claim requires an end-to-end verified path and is suppressed when EQ, gain, crossfeed, mixing, or unsupported conversion is active. Peak/RMS values are analysis measurements, not a guarantee of analog output level.

## 8. End-to-end user flows

### 8.1 First import

1. Welcome screen explains local-only indexing and no automatic playback.
2. User chooses a folder or files; host permission prompt is separate and explicit.
3. Indexing starts incrementally; existing results remain usable.
4. Progress shows processed/total when known; indeterminate progress is labeled when total is unknown.
5. Unsupported, permission-denied, and missing files appear in a review list.
6. Cancel stops indexing and keeps completed results; it does not delete audio.
7. Library ready; user presses Play deliberately.

**Failure exits:** permission denied → explain access and retry; disconnected drive → mark source offline; partial decode issues → keep valid tracks.

### 8.2 Play and queue

1. User chooses a track/album or presses Play on a context.
2. Loading state appears; transport and identity update together.
3. Playing state updates all modes and the signal.
4. “Play next” adds an item and announces the new count; undo is available.
5. Queue panel shows explicit items and “Then resumes at …”.
6. Reorder by drag handle or `Alt+Up/Down`; insertion line and announcement confirm the move.
7. Remove/clear is non-destructive and undoable.

### 8.3 Batch tag edit

1. Select rows; selection toolbar appears.
2. Open Edit metadata; mixed values remain “Multiple values.”
3. Changed fields are marked; untouched mixed fields stay untouched.
4. Artwork replacement and numbering are separate choices.
5. Save writes supported embedded tags; filename renaming is not implied.
6. Per-file failures retain form edits and identify the affected files.
7. Unsupported fields are read-only with an explanation.

### 8.4 Skin change

1. Open Skin Studio; choose an installed skin or import a data-only package.
2. Preview tokens in desktop/compact/mobile variants.
3. Validate contrast, target sizes, required slots, font fallback, and schema version.
4. Apply explicitly; previous skin remains available for undo.
5. Invalid skin is rejected without changing the current skin.
6. Restore defaults is always reachable.

### 8.5 Sleep timer

1. Choose a preset or custom duration.
2. Choose outcome: fade then pause, pause at end of track, or another supported action.
3. Confirm; timer badge shows remaining time and outcome.
4. Cancel restores normal playback without changing files.
5. System shutdown/hibernate is a separate permission-gated feature, never the default timer outcome.

### 8.6 Error recovery

1. Playback pauses safely; current item and queue are preserved.
2. Persistent alert identifies the file/problem and likely cause.
3. Locate file, retry, skip, or copy diagnostics are explicit.
4. Diagnostics exclude audio contents and private paths by default.
5. Skip advances according to queue/context rules; it does not clear the queue.

## 9. Layout system, responsive behavior, and modes

### Reference canvases

| Surface | Canvas | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Desktop workspace | 1440 × 960 | Flagship layout and redlines |
| Medium workspace | 1100 × 820 | Tablet/small desktop reflow |
| Compact desktop | 720 × 760 content region | Single-column behavior |
| Mini player | 420 × 248 | Small persistent player |
| Shade strip | 560 × 72 | Minimal transport + identity |
| Classic stack | 880 px reference width; 560 px minimum | Player/EQ/playlist modules |
| Mobile | 390 × 844 | Touch-first concept |

These are logical-pixel design references, not fixed production window sizes. Production reflows content and permits vertical scrolling; it does not uniformly scale the desktop UI down.

### Desktop grid

- Sidebar: 224 px at the flagship reference.
- Content gutter: 24 px; internal region gaps: 24–32 px.
- Now Playing artwork: 328 px reference; identity column fluid; queue: 480 px reference.
- Signal region spans content width; transport is fixed at the bottom.
- Panel radius: 12–14 px; control radius: 8–10 px; pill radius: half height.
- Base spacing: 4 px; common steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64.

### Reflow rules

- ≥1200: sidebar + content + optional queue column.
- 900–1199: labeled tabs; artwork/identity and queue stack or share a row when space allows.
- <900: single column; queue opens as a sheet; transport remains persistent.
- Mobile: artwork scales to available width; metadata wraps; secondary actions move to labeled overflow only when necessary.
- At 200% text size, action labels wrap or controls grow vertically; no clipped primary actions.
- Long titles truncate visually with full value in details/accessible name; primary action labels never truncate.
- RTL mirrors navigation and row order, but time progression and transport direction follow locale/media conventions and are tested explicitly.

### Mode contract

| Mode | Keeps | Adds / changes | Must not do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workspace | Full library + transport | Queue/signal regions | Hide core playback |
| Focus | Identity + signal + transport | Large visualization, exit | Trap without Esc/back |
| Mini | Identity + transport + expand | Compact signal | Clear queue or lose state |
| Shade | Identity + essential transport + expand | Minimal height | Hide expand or shrink targets below policy |
| Classic | Same objects/state | Modular stack, metal texture | Change queue semantics or use legacy tiny targets |

## 10. Visual language and design tokens

### Semantic palette — Studio Dark

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `surface.canvas` | `#101519` | Deepest background |
| `surface.shell` | `#151C21` | App shell / sidebar |
| `surface.panel` | `#1B242B` | Panels and transport |
| `surface.raised` | `#243139` | Hover / selected / raised controls |
| `border.default` | `#35454E` | Subtle separation; not sole control boundary |
| `text.primary` | `#F3F7F6` | Main text |
| `text.secondary` | `#ADBDC5` | Metadata / supporting text |
| `text.tertiary` | `#84969F` | Low-emphasis labels; validate on actual surface |
| `accent.primary` | `#79E3C2` | Primary action / active signal |
| `accent.on-primary` | `#10251F` | Text/icon on mint |
| `accent.secondary` | `#F3C580` | Warm highlight / peaks |
| `info` | `#91BFFF` | Informational accent |
| `warning` | `#F3C580` | Attention; paired with icon/text |
| `danger` | `#FF9B9B` | Error/destructive; paired with message |
| `focus.ring` | `#FFFFFF` | High-contrast focus indicator |

### Daylight mapping

Canvas `#E9EFEE`; shell `#F7FAF9`; panel `#FFFFFF`; raised `#E7EFED`; text `#172B27`; secondary text `#4E655F`; accent `#116B53`; on-accent `#FFFFFF`; warning `#8B530D`; danger `#A32D38`. Light theme uses darker semantic colors rather than inverting dark-theme accents.

### High Contrast mapping

Canvas/shell `#000000`; panel `#101010`; raised `#202020`; border `#BDBDBD`; text `#FFFFFF`; secondary `#E0E0E0`; accent `#A8FFDA`; on-accent `#000000`. The same components and layout are retained.

### Typography

- Primary: Inter / system sans fallback (`SF Pro Display`, `Segoe UI`, Arial, sans-serif).
- Numerals/time/code: JetBrains Mono / SFMono-Regular / Consolas / monospace; tabular numerals.
- Scale: display 40/54; screen title 28/38; section 18/24; body 14/20; metadata 12/16; overline 11/14.
- Weights: 400 body, 500 labels, 600 section/action, 650–750 display/brand where supported.
- SVG sources use live text for editability. Production may use native text; export outlines only for final static artwork if font licensing and editing requirements allow.

### Elevation and texture

- Default: tonal surfaces + 1 px borders; shadows are optional and never the only boundary.
- Classic: original vector bevel gradient, restrained highlights, no copied bitmap sprites.
- Album art: original vector geometry; real user artwork is raster-safe inside a vector frame.
- No glass blur over dense text; no continuous background animation behind reading content.

## 11. Reusable component inventory and state contracts

### 11.1 Component registry

| ID | Component | Variants | Required states | Key rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Button | Primary, secondary, quiet, destructive | Default, hover, focus, pressed, disabled, loading | 40 px desktop / 44 touch; label or accessible name |
| C02 | Icon button | Ghost, solid, active | Default, hover, focus, pressed, disabled | 40/44 wrapper; tooltip + accessible name |
| C03 | Split button | Primary + menu | Closed, open, focused, disabled | Menu does not change primary meaning |
| C04 | Segmented control | 2–4 options | Selected, unselected, focus, disabled | Selected uses tint + weight/position |
| C05 | Tabs | Workspace, library, settings | Active, hover, focus, overflow | Labels persist; arrow-key navigation |
| C06 | Navigation item | Sidebar, header, mobile | Default, active, hover, focus | Icon + label; empty destination remains usable |
| C07 | Search field | Inline, command | Empty, typed, loading, results, no results, error | Typing never auto-plays |
| C08 | Text field | Default, numeric, multiline | Default, focus, filled, error, disabled, read-only | Label outside; error identifies correction |
| C09 | Select / combobox | Native-like, searchable | Closed, open, selected, focus, unavailable | Capability unavailable explained |
| C10 | Checkbox | Unchecked, checked, mixed | Focus, disabled | Mixed never silently overwrites |
| C11 | Radio | Unselected, selected | Focus, disabled | One choice in group |
| C12 | Switch | On, off | Focus, disabled, pending | State label; pending not shown as applied |
| C13 | Slider | Seek, volume, EQ, preamp | Default, hover, focus, drag, disabled | Value text; keyboard steps; min/max |
| C14 | Rating | 0–5 stars | Empty, partial, full, focus | Accessible value; not color-only |
| C15 | Badge | Format, quality, queue, live, offline | Neutral, soft, warning, error | Short factual text; details available |
| C16 | Transport | Full, compact, shade | Empty, loading, playing, paused, buffering, error | Shared state; stable geometry |
| C17 | Track row | Default, current, selected, queued, unavailable | Hover, focus, drag, drop-target | Current ≠ selected ≠ queued |
| C18 | Album card | Grid, compact | Default, hover, focus, unavailable | Play action explicit; card opens details |
| C19 | Queue item | Pending, current, resume | Hover, focus, drag, removing | Handle + remove; non-destructive |
| C20 | Playlist row | Standard, smart, offline | Default, active, focus, editing | Type and availability visible |
| C21 | Progress | Determinate, indeterminate | Running, paused, canceled, complete | Label; cancel when supported |
| C22 | Alert | Info, success, warning, error | Inline, persistent, dismissible | Error persists; undo when useful |
| C23 | Toast | Success, undo, info | Enter, hover/focus, dismiss | Never sole error record |
| C24 | Dialog | Confirm, form, chooser | Open, focus, submitting, error | Focus trap; Esc/cancel; return focus |
| C25 | Menu / popover | Context, overflow, select | Open, focus, disabled item | One top layer; predictable close |
| C26 | Tooltip | Label, shortcut, explanation | Delayed, focus-visible | Not sole carrier of critical info |
| C27 | Empty state | Library, search, lyrics, queue | Empty, loading, offline | One primary next action |
| C28 | Signal | Wave, spectrum, scope, static | Live, paused, frozen, unavailable | Pause visuals ≠ pause audio |
| C29 | Skin card | Installed, preview, invalid | Default, selected, hover, focus | Validation before apply |
| C30 | Token field | Color, number, enum | Valid, invalid, pending | Semantic name; contrast feedback |
| C31 | Shortcut row | Default, recording, conflict | Focus, conflict, saved | Conflict before save; restore defaults |
| C32 | Timer chip | Duration, outcome | Running, paused, expired | Outcome explicit; cancel reachable |
| C33 | Source row | Available, offline, permission | Default, focus, removing | Remove source ≠ delete files |
| C34 | Capability row | Supported, unsupported, unknown | Available, disabled, checking | Never fake an enabled toggle |
| C35 | Window/mode control | Mini, shade, focus, expand | Default, focus, unavailable | Exit always reachable |

### 11.2 Interaction geometry

- Minimum pointer target: 24 × 24 CSS px, consistent with WCAG 2.2 Target Size (Minimum); design defaults are 40 px desktop and 44 px touch. [8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
- Icon glyph: 20–24 px inside a 40/44 px wrapper.
- Track row: 56 px default; compact desktop may use 48 px; touch does not go below 44 px.
- Button: 40 px high, 9 px radius, 14 px horizontal padding; icon 18 px + 10 px gap.
- Focus ring: 2 px, 2 px offset, drawn above state tint; never removed.
- Drag handle: visible grip; keyboard alternative `Alt+Up/Down`; insertion line plus announcement.
- Sliders: Arrow = small step; Page = larger step; Home/End = bounds; numeric value available.

### 11.3 State layering

1. Surface token.
2. Hover/selected/pressed tint.
3. Content: icon, label, value.
4. Focus ring.
5. Drag insertion/error message.

Disabled controls reduce emphasis but retain readable explanation. Loading controls preserve geometry and expose a busy state; they do not silently change action meaning.

## 12. Waveform, spectrum, and motion system

### 12.1 Four presentation modes

| Mode | Data | Best use | Truthfulness rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mirrored waveform | Time-domain envelope / amplitude history | Default listening and seek context | Played/unplayed distinction; no fake live motion |
| Spectrum | FFT magnitudes grouped into log-spaced bands | Classic performance view | Label analysis; peak caps decay honestly |
| Oscilloscope | Time-domain samples | Signal inspection | Stable centerline; clipping indicator separate |
| Static / reduced motion | Artwork + optional numeric state | Accessibility / low power | No continuous motion; audio unaffected |

### 12.2 Data pipeline

```text
Decoder / source
  → optional DSP chain
  → analysis tap (post-processing, pre-output where supported)
  → bounded ring buffers
  → UI aggregation worker / throttled bridge
  → SVG path / rect / transform updates
  → output device
```

- Audio rendering remains on the audio thread; UI work never blocks it.
- Web demonstration uses `AnalyserNode` time-domain and frequency data. MDN documents `getFloatTimeDomainData` and `getFloatFrequencyData` for these purposes. [9](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AnalyserNode)
- Native implementations use an equivalent analysis tap and a bounded queue; they do not copy entire audio buffers to the UI.
- Analysis point is labeled. Post-DSP analysis does not prove the final device output format.
- When no fresh data exists, freeze the last frame and label it; do not generate random “live” bars.

### 12.3 Visual update budget

- Target: 30 fps visual updates on desktop; 20 fps in compact/low-power mode; static when paused or hidden.
- Aggregate to 96–192 waveform columns and 32–64 spectrum bands for typical panels; scale down on compact surfaces.
- Reuse SVG nodes and update attributes; do not rebuild the entire SVG tree every frame.
- Use a ring buffer for history; bound memory and drop old visual frames rather than audio.
- Pause when the document/window is hidden; resume with fresh data, not stale animation.
- Reduced motion defaults to static or low-rate numeric updates; no flashing, strobing, rotation, or camera zoom.
- Visualization pause is separate from audio pause and is always reachable in focus view.

### 12.4 Seeking versus signal pause

- Seek slider: changes playback position; drag previews time, release commits.
- Signal pause: stops visual updates only.
- Static mode: replaces animated presentation without changing playback.
- Live streams: disable file-style seeking and duration; show live/buffering state instead.

### 12.5 SVG production contract

- Root SVG has `viewBox`, title/desc for meaningful artwork, and stable IDs.
- Decorative layers are hidden from assistive technology; interactive controls have native/HTML semantics.
- Use `path`, `rect`, `circle`, `line`, `text`, `clipPath`, gradients, and symbols; no external scripts in skin assets.
- Waveform group exposes `data-role="signal"` and mode/state attributes.
- Skin tokens map to fills/strokes through a controlled theme layer; arbitrary CSS/JS injection is forbidden.
- Static design SVGs are illustrative frames. The interactive lab is the only artifact that claims live audio-driven updates.

## 13. Skin architecture and white-label contract

### 13.1 What a skin may change

- Semantic colors, approved typography scale/family fallback, radius, border weight, texture, vector artwork, logo slot, signal palette, and approved layout variant.
- Density within locked minimum target sizes.
- Decorative bevels/gradients in Classic mode.

### 13.2 What a skin may not change

- Control meaning, queue semantics, playback state truth, focus order, minimum targets, error honesty, privacy defaults, or permission boundaries.
- Add executable scripts, remote fetches, arbitrary HTML, or new privileged actions.
- Remove labels from core navigation or hide the exit from compact/focus modes.

### 13.3 Package structure

```text
brand-skin/
├── manifest.json       # schema version, id, name, version, capabilities
├── tokens.json         # semantic values only
├── assets/
│   ├── logo.svg        # optional white-label mark
│   ├── texture.svg     # optional decorative vector texture
│   └── fallback-art.svg
└── preview.svg         # optional static preview
```

### 13.4 Validation pipeline

1. Parse JSON against schema; reject unknown executable fields.
2. Check schema version and required semantic tokens.
3. Resolve colors and compute contrast against actual adjacent surfaces.
4. Validate radius/density bounds and required layout slots.
5. Sanitize SVG assets: no scripts, event handlers, external references, or foreign objects.
6. Render preview in desktop/compact/mobile variants.
7. Run focus/target/overflow checks.
8. Apply only after explicit confirmation; keep previous skin for undo.

### 13.5 White-label slots

- `brand.logo`, `brand.wordmark`, `brand.productName`, `brand.accent`, `brand.surface`, `brand.signalPalette`.
- Default demonstration brand is FUSE; replace all brand strings and logo geometry through tokens/assets, not by editing component behavior.
- Legal/trademark clearance for a final brand is outside this design study.

### 13.6 Classic skin specifics

- Original metal gradient and bevel geometry; no Winamp sprite extraction.
- Player/EQ/playlist modules share the same store as workspace mode.
- Minimum logical width 560 px; reference stack 880 px.
- EQ bands retain numeric values and reset; playlist rows retain readable labels and modern targets.
- Shade mode keeps essential transport and expand; it is not a pixel-perfect legacy clone.

## 14. Accessibility and inclusive interaction

### Normative targets

- Text contrast ≥4.5:1 for normal text; large text ≥3:1, with documented exceptions. [7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- Meaningful control boundaries/state indicators and focus indicators ≥3:1 against adjacent colors where required. [10](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)
- Pointer targets ≥24 × 24 CSS px minimum; default 40/44 px. [8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
- Moving/auto-updating content has pause/stop/hide control; reduced motion is respected. [11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html)
- Core playback remains usable at 200% text size and compact equivalent width; test 400% zoom reflow behavior.

### Keyboard contract

| Key | Action | Scope / guard |
|---|---|---|
| Space | Play/pause | Not while typing or activating a focused button |
| Left/Right | Seek ±5 s | Seekable media only |
| Shift+Left/Right | Seek ±30 s | Clamp to bounds |
| Up/Down | Volume ±1% | When transport region is focused |
| M | Mute/unmute | Not while typing |
| Q | Add selection to queue | Announce count + undo |
| Alt+Up/Down | Reorder queue item | Focused queue item only |
| Ctrl/⌘+F | Search | Focus search field |
| Ctrl/⌘+, | Settings | Preserve return focus |
| Esc | Close top layer | Then leave focus view; never quit app |
| ? | Shortcut reference | Not while typing |

All bindings are remappable; conflicts are detected before save. OS media keys remain host-managed unless a separately permitted global-shortcut integration exists.

### Assistive technology contract

- SVG is presentation; production controls are native buttons/inputs or correctly roled HTML/SVG hybrids.
- Every icon button has an accessible name; decorative SVG is hidden.
- Sliders expose min/max/current value and units.
- Queue changes announce item, new position, and count; not every animation frame.
- Current track changes announce once; buffering/error changes announce once.
- Modal dialogs trap focus, close with Esc/cancel, and return focus to the invoker.
- Focus is never obscured by sticky transport or overlays.
- Color is reinforced by text, icon, shape, or position.

### Motion and sensory safety

- No flashing/strobing; no rapid full-screen luminance changes.
- Reduced motion: static artwork or low-rate numeric signal; no slide/bounce/pulse.
- Hover/focus pauses toast dismissal; errors remain persistent.
- Audio never starts automatically on import, skin apply, or mode change.

## 15. Content, error, empty, and recovery design

### Voice and terminology

- Use “Play next,” “Add to queue,” “Then resumes at,” “Remove from playlist,” “Delete file,” “Source quality,” “Output device,” “Pause visualization.”
- Avoid ambiguous “Add,” “Remove,” “HD,” “Lossless output,” or “Live” without context.
- Error copy: what happened → what remains safe → what the user can do.
- Counts are explicit: “3 explicit tracks,” “8 tracks · 34 min,” “1,668 of 2,418 files indexed.”

### Empty states

| Surface | Message pattern | Primary action |
|---|---|---|
| Library | No albums yet; choose a folder | Choose folder |
| Search | No local matches; check spelling or filters | Clear filters |
| Queue | No explicit items; context resumes | Add selected / open library |
| Lyrics | No embedded lyrics; add local file | Add lyrics file |
| History | No listening history yet | Play something |
| Radio offline | Station unavailable; local library remains | Retry / return to library |

### Error taxonomy

- Missing file → locate/skip; preserve queue.
- Unsupported codec → explain format support; keep valid library items.
- Permission denied → explain access; retry after permission.
- Decode failure → retry/skip; diagnostics on request.
- Tag write failure → retain edits; identify files.
- Device unavailable → keep current route or choose another; warn about brief pause.
- Skin invalid → reject; keep current skin.
- Stream reconnecting → show attempt/buffer state; retry/local fallback.

### Destructive boundaries

- Remove from playlist ≠ remove source folder ≠ delete audio file.
- Clear history ≠ clear favorites ≠ clear queue.
- Clear cache ≠ remove indexed library.
- System shutdown is never the default sleep-timer outcome.
- Confirmation dialogs name the exact scope and offer a safe default.

### Screen-by-screen acceptance notes

- **01 Now Playing:** artwork, identity, source badges, explicit queue, signal, and persistent transport must remain distinct; queue preview opens the full queue.
- **02 Album library:** grid/list/sort/filter/import are visible; card play is explicit; no recommendation-service assumption.
- **03 Track selection:** selection toolbar acts on selected rows, not the current track; current/selected/queued styling remains separate.
- **04 Queue:** explicit items and resume context are simultaneously visible; removal is non-destructive; reorder has keyboard equivalent.
- **05 Focus view:** large signal, pause-visuals control, exit, and stable metadata; Esc returns without changing playback.
- **06 EQ:** numeric bands, preset, reset, preamp, processing summary; unsupported effects are not shown as active.
- **07 Skin studio:** preview and apply are separate; imported skins are data-only; installed skins retain restore path.
- **08 Audio settings:** output route, gapless, resume, queue persistence, normalization; capability-gated advanced routing.
- **09 Tag editor:** mixed values, explicit save, artwork choice, permission review; tag write ≠ filename rename.
- **10 Search:** local results, type grouping, keyboard navigation; typing does not play; remote search is opt-in.
- **11 Onboarding:** deliberate folder/file choice; no account/upload/auto-play; empty transport explains absence.
- **12 Recovery:** missing file and partial import issues; locate/skip/diagnostics; queue/library preserved.
- **13 Daylight:** same anatomy with light semantic tokens; no contrast inversion shortcut.
- **14 Classic:** original metal stack; player/EQ/playlist modules; modern targets and labels.
- **15 Mini/shade:** shared state, essential transport, labeled expand; no queue loss on resize.
- **16 Mobile:** touch-first player/library/queue; 44 px targets; native safe areas remain host work.
- **17 Medium:** labeled tabs and reflowed regions; no horizontal core-task scrolling.
- **18 Sleep timer:** duration + outcome; pause is default; shutdown is separate.
- **19 Radio:** saved URLs, reconnect state, no file-style seek/duration claims.
- **20 Details/lyrics:** source facts separate from output; local lyrics empty state.
- **21 History:** local record, explicit clear, separate favorites; no implicit scrobbling.
- **22 Import:** incremental progress, pause/cancel, partial results retained, no file modification.
- **23 Desktop wireframe:** region hierarchy before decoration.

## 17. Implementation architecture and handoff

### 17.1 Recommended separation

```text
Host adapters (macOS / Windows / Linux / web / mobile)
  ├─ file permissions / dialogs / media session / safe areas
  └─ audio backend capability registry

Core domain
  ├─ library index / metadata / playlists / smart rules
  ├─ playback state machine
  ├─ explicit queue + context pointer
  ├─ favorites / history / settings
  └─ skin validation / token resolution

Audio engine
  ├─ decode / buffer / output route
  ├─ DSP / gain / limiter
  └─ analysis tap → bounded visual frames

Presentation
  ├─ native/HTML semantic controls
  ├─ SVG signal and vector artwork
  ├─ layout variants / modes
  └─ accessibility announcements / focus management
```

### 17.2 Suggested state shape

```ts
type PlaybackState =
  | 'empty' | 'loading' | 'playing' | 'paused'
  | 'buffering' | 'stopped' | 'error';

interface PlayerStore {
  playback: PlaybackState;
  current?: TrackRef;
  positionMs: number;
  durationMs?: number;       // undefined for live streams
  seekable: boolean;
  context?: { id: string; kind: 'album'|'playlist'|'folder'; index: number; order: TrackRef[] };
  explicitQueue: TrackRef[];
  shuffle: boolean;
  repeat: 'off' | 'all' | 'one';
  volume: number;            // 0..1
  muted: boolean;
  output?: OutputCapability;
  sourceFacts?: SourceFacts;
  processing: ProcessingSummary;
  error?: RecoverableError;
}

interface VisualFrame {
  timestampMs: number;
  mode: 'wave' | 'spectrum' | 'scope' | 'static';
  waveform?: Float32Array;   // aggregated envelope
  spectrum?: Float32Array;   // dB or normalized magnitudes
  peak?: number;
  clipping?: boolean;
  stale: boolean;
}
```

### 17.3 SVG rendering guidance

- Keep one SVG root per signal region; reuse child nodes.
- Waveform: update `d` on a path or `y/height` on a bounded set of rects.
- Spectrum: update rect heights/transforms; use log-spaced aggregation.
- Scope: update a path from a decimated sample window.
- Use `clipPath` for artwork and signal bounds; avoid overflow into neighboring controls.
- Use semantic IDs prefixed per component instance to prevent gradient/clip collisions.
- Do not put production text into outlined paths unless exporting static artwork; keep live text for localization and accessibility.
- Raster album art may be embedded in a framed image element in production; the design package uses original vector sleeves.

### 17.4 Performance targets

| Area | Target | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Library list | Smooth scroll at 100k tracks | Virtualization, indexed queries |
| Import | UI remains usable | Incremental indexing, cancellable worker |
| Signal | 30 fps desktop / 20 fps compact | Node reuse, bounded aggregation |
| Audio | No UI-induced dropouts | Audio thread isolation, drop visual frames |
| Search | Responsive local results | Debounced indexed query, stale-result labeling |
| Skin apply | No layout shift in core controls | Token swap, prevalidated variants |
| Startup | Restore state without auto-play | Persisted store, explicit play |

### 17.5 Security and privacy

- Skins are data-only: JSON tokens + sanitized SVG assets. Reject scripts, event handlers, external URLs, foreignObject, and executable fields.
- Imported SVG is sanitized and rendered in a restricted context; no network fetch from skin assets.
- Diagnostics are opt-in and redact private paths/audio contents by default.
- Remote metadata/artwork/scrobbling/providers are opt-in and labeled.
- File deletion, renaming, tag writes, and system shutdown require separate explicit actions/permissions.
- Source-folder removal stops indexing that source; it does not delete audio files.

### 17.6 Handoff checklist

- [ ] Resolve final brand name/logo and legal clearance.
- [ ] Confirm target platforms and audio backend capability matrix.
- [ ] Implement semantic control layer beneath SVG presentation.
- [ ] Wire playback state machine and explicit queue store.
- [ ] Implement analysis tap and bounded visual frames.
- [ ] Implement token resolver and skin validator.
- [ ] Add localization/RTL/long-string fixtures.
- [ ] Run keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, and motion audits.
- [ ] Run 100k-track library and audio/visual performance tests.
- [ ] Complete usability tasks for import, queue, tags, skins, and recovery.

## 18. Validation plan and acceptance criteria

### 18.1 Design QA performed in this package

- 50 SVG artifacts generated and parsed as valid XML.
- Representative screens rendered to PNG for visual inspection.
- Corrected artwork clipping, control overlap, empty-player semantics, theme leakage, and icon-sheet overflow during render review.
- All artwork is original vector geometry; no reference-product sprites or logos are embedded.
- Static frames are explicitly labeled as illustrations; live behavior is delegated to the waveform lab.

### 18.2 Contrast spot checks (computed, not a certification)

| Pair | Studio Dark | Daylight | Requirement / note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Primary text / panel | 14.58:1 | 14.88:1 | Passes normal-text threshold |
| Secondary text / panel | 8.14:1 | 6.27:1 | Passes normal-text threshold |
| Tertiary text / panel | 5.13:1 | 4.92:1 | Passes normal-text threshold |
| Accent / panel | 10.18:1 | 6.46:1 | Passes meaningful-graphic threshold |
| On-accent / accent | 10.39:1 | 6.46:1 | Passes normal-text threshold |
| Danger / panel | 7.81:1 | 7.02:1 | Passes normal-text threshold |
| Default border / panel | 1.58:1 | 1.77:1 | Decorative/subtle; not sole control boundary |

**Important:** subtle borders are not sufficient as the only identifier of a control. Interactive controls must also use readable text/icons, state shapes, or a stronger boundary/focus indicator. Tertiary text on raised surfaces can fall below 4.5:1 in some combinations; production must validate each actual pairing and promote text to secondary where needed. These spot checks do not constitute WCAG conformance.

### 18.3 Required test matrix

| Test | Acceptance criterion |
|---|---|
| Import permission denied | Explain access; no silent scan; retry available |
| Partial import | Valid tracks usable; issues listed; cancel keeps completed work |
| Queue vs context | Explicit items consumed first; resume point visible |
| Queue reorder | Pointer and keyboard produce same order; announcement correct |
| Queue removal/clear | Files/library unchanged; undo available |
| Mode switch | Workspace/focus/mini/shade/Classic share state and queue |
| Seek | Keyboard steps, drag preview, bounds, live-stream disable |
| EQ | Numeric values, reset, preset, preamp, clipping warning |
| Output change | Capability check; brief-pause warning; no false fidelity claim |
| Tag batch | Mixed values preserved; explicit save; per-file failure retains edits |
| Skin import | Invalid/schema/script assets rejected; current skin unchanged |
| Skin contrast | Default skins pass; invalid custom skin blocked or explicit override |
| Visual pause | Visual updates stop; audio continues |
| Reduced motion | Static/low-rate presentation; no flashing |
| Keyboard | All core tasks reachable; focus visible; Esc closes top layer |
| Screen reader | Names/roles/values/states correct; announcements not per-frame |
| Zoom/reflow | 200% text and compact width preserve core tasks |
| Long strings/RTL | No clipped actions; full identity available; mirrored layout tested |
| Offline/disconnect | Local playback remains; remote/source marked unavailable |
| Large library | 100k tracks scroll/search without UI stall |
| Audio/visual load | No audio dropouts caused by visual rendering |

### 18.4 Usability tasks

1. Import a folder and play one track without creating an account.
2. Add two tracks to Play next, reorder them, and identify what plays afterward.
3. Remove a track from a playlist without deleting the file.
4. Edit a mixed album field without overwriting unrelated mixed values.
5. Switch to Classic/mini and return without losing the queue.
6. Pause the visualization while audio continues.
7. Apply a skin and restore the previous one.
8. Recover from a missing file by locating or skipping it.
9. Set a 30-minute fade-to-pause timer and cancel it.
10. Complete core playback using keyboard only.

## 19. Delivery roadmap and open decisions

### Phase 0 — Decisions before production

- Final brand/name/logo and trademark clearance.
- Primary platform order: macOS/Windows/Linux/web/mobile.
- Audio backend and capability matrix.
- Local database and playlist portability policy.
- Provider/privacy policy and premium boundary, if any.
- Skin distribution/security policy.

### Phase 1 — Core player

- Semantic shell, transport, state machine, local import, library, queue, search, recovery.
- Dark/light/high-contrast tokens; keyboard/focus/zoom baseline.
- Static signal placeholder and real analysis tap.

### Phase 2 — Differentiators

- Focus/mini/shade/Classic modes; reactive SVG modes.
- EQ/presets/output chooser; sleep timer.
- Skin studio/token editor/import validation.
- Smart playlists, favorites/history, tag editor.

### Phase 3 — Conditional depth

- Radio/podcasts/providers; advanced DSP/output; mobile native integrations.
- Converter/CD/recording/scheduler only after backend/legal review.
- Localization/RTL expansion and performance hardening.

### Open decisions register

| Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Default EQ depth | 10-band vs 20-band | 10-band default; 20-band advanced capability |
| Classic default | Optional vs default | Optional; workspace default |
| Signal default | Wave vs spectrum | Mirrored wave; spectrum in Classic/focus |
| Queue persistence | Always vs setting | Setting, default on for local player |
| Remote providers | Built-in vs extensions | Extensions, opt-in |
| Skin format | Legacy bitmap vs token SVG | Token SVG; legacy import as research only |
| Mobile scope | Responsive concept vs native | Concept now; native after platform decision |
| Brand | FUSE demo vs final | White-label slots; final brand pending |

## 20. Source notes and limitations

### Reference sources

1. VOX Mac Music Player product page — compact/album-led presentation, formats, EQ, gapless, output and source features. https://vox.rocks/mac-music-player
2. AIMP official desktop features — library, playlists, queue, EQ/DSP, normalization, tagging, skins and scheduler breadth. https://www.aimp.ru/?do=features
3. Winamp Desktop Player help — playlist, EQ, skins, color themes, classic/modern skin support. https://support.winamp.com/winamp-desktop-player-for-windows
4. Winamp Skin Museum / classic skin tutorial — classic skin configuration concepts such as visualization and playlist color mappings. https://winampskins.neocities.org/config
5. Webamp documentation entry point — classic-player implementation reference. https://docs.webamp.org/
6. W3C WAI — WCAG 2.2 contrast, non-text contrast, target size, and pause/stop/hide understanding pages. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/
7. MDN — AnalyserNode time-domain and frequency-data APIs. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AnalyserNode

### Interpretation rules

- Reference products inspire interaction patterns; no proprietary assets are copied.
- Public pages are not a substitute for version-specific testing.
- Premium, platform, and plugin differences are treated as capability gates.
- Accessibility targets are design requirements; formal conformance requires implementation testing.
- The interactive waveform lab demonstrates browser audio analysis, not a production audio engine.
- Fictional metadata and original vector sleeves avoid implying real artist endorsements or licensed album art.

### License and reuse note

The design specification and original SVG artwork are provided as project deliverables for adaptation. Third-party fonts used for rendering checks are Inter and JetBrains Mono; their licenses are included in the package font directory when present. Final production font embedding/redistribution must follow the applicable font license. Reference-product names are used only for analysis and attribution.

  "$schema": "./skin.schema.json",

  "id": "fuse-studio-dark",

  "version": "1.0.0",
  "brand": {
    "productName": "FUSE",
    "wordmark": "FUSE",
    "logoSlot": "assets/logo.svg"
  },
  "layout": {
    "variant": "workspace",
    "density": "comfortable",
    "minTargetPx": 24,
    "defaultDesktopTargetPx": 40,
    "defaultTouchTargetPx": 44,
    "radiusPanelPx": 12,
    "radiusControlPx": 9,
    "baseSpacingPx": 4
  },
  "typography": {
    "family": "Inter, 'SF Pro Display', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif",
    "monoFamily": "'JetBrains Mono', 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, monospace",
    "scale": { "display": 40, "screen": 28, "section": 18, "body": 14, "metadata": 12, "overline": 11 }
  },
  "colors": {
    "surface": { "canvas": "#101519", "shell": "#151C21", "panel": "#1B242B", "raised": "#243139" },
    "border": { "default": "#35454E", "strong": "#84969F" },
    "text": { "primary": "#F3F7F6", "secondary": "#ADBDC5", "tertiary": "#84969F", "onAccent": "#10251F" },
    "accent": { "primary": "#79E3C2", "secondary": "#F3C580", "info": "#91BFFF" },
    "status": { "warning": "#F3C580", "danger": "#FF9B9B", "success": "#79E3C2" },
    "focus": { "ring": "#FFFFFF" },
    "signal": { "played": "#79E3C2", "unplayed": "#84969F", "peak": "#F3C580", "grid": "#35454E" }
  },
  "motion": { "default": "full", "reducedMotion": "static", "visualFpsDesktop": 30, "visualFpsCompact": 20, "allowFlashing": false },
  "locked": {
    "controlMeanings": true,
    "queueSemantics": true,
    "focusOrder": true,
    "minimumTargets": true,
    "errorHonesty": true,
    "privacyDefaults": true,
    "executableSkinCode": false
  }
}

### `skin.schema.json`

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://example.invalid/fuse/skin.schema.json",
  "title": "FUSE data-only skin manifest",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["schemaVersion", "id", "name", "version", "layout", "colors", "locked"],
  "properties": {
    "$schema": { "type": "string" },
    "schemaVersion": { "const": "1.0.0" },
    "id": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$" },
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 80 },
    "version": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$" },
    "brand": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "productName": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 },
        "wordmark": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 },
        "logoSlot": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^assets/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\\.svg$" }
      }
    },
    "layout": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["variant", "minTargetPx", "defaultDesktopTargetPx", "defaultTouchTargetPx"],
      "properties": {
        "variant": { "enum": ["workspace", "classic", "mini", "shade"] },
        "density": { "enum": ["compact", "comfortable"] },
        "minTargetPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 24, "maximum": 64 },
        "defaultDesktopTargetPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 40, "maximum": 64 },
        "defaultTouchTargetPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 44, "maximum": 72 },
        "radiusPanelPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 24 },
        "radiusControlPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 16 },
        "baseSpacingPx": { "type": "number", "minimum": 4, "maximum": 8 }
      }
    },
    "typography": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "family": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 },
        "monoFamily": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 },
        "scale": {
          "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "display": { "type": "number", "minimum": 28, "maximum": 56 },
            "screen": { "type": "number", "minimum": 22, "maximum": 36 },
            "section": { "type": "number", "minimum": 16, "maximum": 24 },
            "body": { "type": "number", "minimum": 14, "maximum": 20 },
            "metadata": { "type": "number", "minimum": 12, "maximum": 16 },
            "overline": { "type": "number", "minimum": 11, "maximum": 14 }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "colors": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["surface", "text", "accent", "focus"],
      "properties": {
        "surface": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "border": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "text": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "accent": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "status": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "focus": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" },
        "signal": { "$ref": "#/$defs/colorGroup" }
      }
    },
    "motion": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "default": { "enum": ["full", "reduced", "static"] },
        "reducedMotion": { "enum": ["static", "low-rate"] },
        "visualFpsDesktop": { "type": "number", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 30 },
        "visualFpsCompact": { "type": "number", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 20 },
        "allowFlashing": { "const": false }
      }
    },
    "locked": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["controlMeanings", "queueSemantics", "focusOrder", "minimumTargets", "errorHonesty", "privacyDefaults", "executableSkinCode"],
      "properties": {
        "controlMeanings": { "const": true },
        "queueSemantics": { "const": true },
        "focusOrder": { "const": true },
        "minimumTargets": { "const": true },
        "errorHonesty": { "const": true },
        "privacyDefaults": { "const": true },
        "executableSkinCode": { "const": false }
      }
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "hexColor": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$" },
    "colorGroup": { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": { "$ref": "#/$defs/hexColor" } }
  }
}

```
